title: Observation of Flat Bands in Type-II Weyl Semimetal TaRhTe$_{4}$
authors: Harry Rankin, Tyler J. Slade, Benjamin Schrunk, Yevhen Kushnirenko, Andrew Eaton, K. U. R. R. S. Rathnayaka, Maxwell Doyle, Lin-Lin Wang, Paul C. Canfield, Adam Kaminski
abstract: Flat bands have been theoretically predicted for decades but have only recently been realized in quantum materials such as magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, kagome and Lieb lattices, and rare-earth metal compounds. To date, only twisted layered materials have enabled tuning of flat-band energies near the electronic chemical potential, thereby influencing transport and thermodynamic properties. Here, we report the presence of flat bands near the chemical potential in bulk TaRhTe$_{4}$, a noncentrosymmetric van-der Waals type-II Weyl semimetal. Flat bands are rarely observed in Weyl semimetals, particularly in nonmagnetic bulk systems, and the observed flat bands were not predicted by density functional theory calculations. TaRhTe$_{4}$ therefore provides a platform in which nontrivial topology coexists with flat bands near the Fermi level, as evidenced by our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements.
summary: This work reports experimental evidence of unexpected flat energy bands in the Weyl semimetal TaRhTe4 using ARPES. The findings highlight a significant discrepancy between theory and experiment, suggesting that topological materials can host emergent electronic states not captured by current computational models. This combination of topology and flat-band physics makes it an interesting platform for condensed matter research.
main_problem: The study aims to observe flat electronic bands near the Fermi level in a noncentrosymmetric bulk Weyl semimetal, as such features are rare and unexpected based on initial theoretical calculations.
main_result: ARPES measurements reveal the presence of distinct, momentum-independent flat bands localized at specific energies below the Fermi level, particularly evident on one crystal surface termination (Termination A).
method: The research combines Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) experiments with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations to probe the electronic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is bulk TaRhTe4, classified as a noncentrosymmetric van-der Waals type-II Weyl semimetal. The analysis compares experimental measurements on different crystal terminations against theoretical predictions.
key_observables: Flat bands near the chemical potential, Fermi surfaces (FSs), and the location/existence of Weyl points (WPs).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (5–5.5 K) for ARPES; energy scales around 4 meV below E_F.
main_assumptions: The flat bands observed were not predicted by initial DFT calculations, suggesting physics beyond the standard theory or surface effects are at play.
figures_summary: Figures compare calculated and measured FSs for two terminations (A and B); Figure 4 specifically highlights the momentum-independent flat bands on Termination A via EDCs/cuts.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the material's topological nature using DFT, presents ARPES data comparing different surface terminations, identifies general agreement with theory, and then focuses heavily on the discrepancy—the unexpected appearance of flat bands in experiment versus calculation.
why_interesting: While focused on topology/band structure, the observation of emergent, unpredicted electronic features like flat bands provides a platform for investigating strong correlation effects or novel many-body physics that standard DFT might miss.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The crystal structure and Brillouin zone of TaRhTe4. a The crystal structure of TaRhTe4. Because it is noncentrosymmetric and layered, there are two different surface terminations, labeled by A and B here. b The Brillouin zone of TaRhTe4.

Figure 2: Fermi surfaces of TaRhTe4. a,b DFT-calculated and ARPES Fermi surfaces for termination B. The green and purple icons show the theoretical momentum positions of the Weyl points. The green WP projections have chirality -1 and the purple WP projections have chirality +1. The squares depict WP projections with predicted energy 13 meV above EF , whereas the circles represent WP projections with energy 50 meV below EF . c,d DFT-calculated and ARPES Fermi surfaces for termination A. Note that in this termination, we obtained data out to ky ≈0.25 1/˚A, whereas for termination B, we only obtained data out to ky ≈0.20 1/˚A.

Figure 3: DFT and ARPES comparison of several energy-momentum cuts near the WP locations on each termination. a-c DFT-calculated energy-momentum cuts through termination B. The purple arrows indicate the theoretical locations of the WPs. d-f ARPES-measured energy-momentum cuts through termination B. The white arrows are placed at the same location as the purple arrows in the DFT calculations. g-i DFT-calculated energy-momentum cuts through termination B. j-l ARPES-measured energy-momentum cuts through termination B. 6

Figure 4: Flat bands in the Fermi surface of termination A. a FS of termination A, showing how the flat bands extend throughout most of the Brillouin zone. b,c,d Several energy-momentum cuts in which the flat bands are visible. The flat bands are shown by the white arrows. e EDCs of panel (b), focused on the area enclosed by the smaller white frame. f EDCs of panel (b) without offset. The individual EDCs are colored distinctly only to highlight that the peaks occur at the same energy for each EDC. The peak of the flat bands occurs approximately 4 meV below the Fermi energy.

Figure 5: Comparison of cuts in each termination near the location of the flat bands a Termination B, where the lowercase roman numerals label the locations of the cuts shown in b i-iv. b Corresponding energy-momentum cuts. No flat bands are seen in termination B. c Termination A, which exhibits the flat bands. The lowercase roman numerals label the locations of the cuts shown in d i-iv. d Energy-momentum cuts at the locations labeled in panel c. The flat bands right below EF are indicated by the white arrows.
